claim: Glutamatergic synapses form the vast majority of connections within neuronal circuits.
source: Glutamatergic synapses form the vast majority of connections within neuronal circuits, but how these subcellular structures are molecularly organized within the mammalian brain is poorly understood.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about the prevalence of glutamatergic synapses in neuronal circuits.

claim: Conventional electron microscopy using chemically fixed, metal-stained tissue has identified a proteinaceous, membrane-associated thickening called the 'postsynaptic density' (PSD).
source: Conventional electron microscopy using chemically fixed, metal-stained tissue has identified a proteinaceous, membrane-associated thickening called the 'postsynaptic density' (PSD).
evidence: This is a citation of established findings from conventional EM studies.

claim: The native glutamatergic synapse did not consistently show a higher density of proteins at the postsynaptic membrane.
source: The native glutamatergic synapse did not consistently show a higher density of proteins at the postsynaptic membrane, thought to be characteristic of the PSD.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the cryoET data presented in the manuscript.

claim: A 'synaptoplasm' consisting of cytoskeletal elements, macromolecular complexes, and membrane-bound organelles extended throughout the pre- and post-synaptic compartments.
source: Instead, a 'synaptoplasm' consisting of cytoskeletal elements, macromolecular complexes, and membrane-bound organelles extended throughout the pre- and post-synaptic compartments.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the cryoET data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Clusters of up to 60 ionotropic glutamate receptors were positioned inside and outside the synaptic cleft.
source: Clusters of up to 60 ionotropic glutamate receptors were positioned inside and outside the synaptic cleft.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the cryoET data presented in the manuscript.

claim: More than a thousand different synaptic proteins have been identified in the mouse and human forebrain.
source: Indeed, more than a thousand different synaptic proteins have been identified in the mouse and human forebrain (Bayés et al., 2011; Roy et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: CryoEM samples must be vitreous and less than ~300 nm thick.
source: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryoEM) has the potential to reveal the native 3-dimensional molecular architecture of mammalian brain synapses, but with the limitation that samples must be vitreous and less than ~300 nm thick.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the technical limitations of cryoEM.

claim: Primary neurons in vitro appear unable to reach the molecular and functional maturity of neurons from the brain itself.
source: Indeed, primary neurons in vitro appear unable to reach the molecular and functional maturity of neurons from the brain itself (Frank et al., 2016; Harris and Pettit, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Microtubules rapidly depolymerize within a matter of 1–3 minutes if the provision of nucleotide triphosphates or cellular integrity becomes compromised.
source: An example is the cytoskeleton, particularly microtubules, which rapidly depolymerize within a matter of 1–3 minutes if the provision of nucleotide triphosphates or cellular integrity becomes compromised (Mitchison, 1995; Pollard and Mooseker, 1981).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Sample preparation from culling to cryopreservation was completed within 2 minutes.
source: 2 min was the time taken to cull, dissect, and cryopreserve samples on EM grids.
evidence: This is a methodological detail describing the sample preparation workflow shown in Figure 1A.

claim: All GFP-positive membranes were attached to a neighbouring membrane, of which 78% were closed compartments and enriched in synaptic vesicles.
source: As expected, all GFP-positive membranes were attached to a neighbouring membrane, of which 78% were closed compartments and enriched in synaptic vesicles that characterize the presynaptic compartment.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the cryoET data analysis.

claim: 96% of presynaptic compartments contained docked synaptic vesicles.
source: All but three of the presynaptic compartments (96%) contained docked synaptic vesicles tethered 2–8 nm from the presynaptic membrane (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the cryoET data analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Filamentous actin networks were present in all PoSM compartments.
source: These were identifiable with a diameter of 7 nm and apparent helical arrangement of subunits (Hanson, 1967) in all PoSM compartments (Okamoto et al., 2007; Figure 1C-E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is a finding from the cryoET data analysis shown in Figure 1C-E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: F-actin was present in 49 ± 7% of PreSM compartments.
source: These were identifiable with a diameter of 7 nm and apparent helical arrangement of subunits (Hanson, 1967) in all PoSM compartments (Okamoto et al., 2007; Figure 1C-E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) and in 49 ± 7% (mean ± SEM, n=5 mice) of PreSM compartments (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the cryoET data analysis shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Microtubules were identified in 15 ± 2% of PreSM compartments.
source: Microtubules were identified (25 nm diameter) in 15 ± 2% of PreSM compartments (Figure 1C, D and F)
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the cryoET data analysis shown in Figure 1C, D and F.

claim: Microtubules were absent from the PoSM.
source: Microtubules were identified (25 nm diameter) in 15 ± 2% of PreSM compartments (Figure 1C, D and F), but as expected, were absent from the PoSM.
evidence: This is a finding from the cryoET data analysis.

claim: Half the population of synapses showed a significant relative increase in molecular density in proximal versus distal regions of cytoplasm in the postsynaptic compartment.
source: The distribution of molecular densities was variable with half the population of synapses showing a significant relative increase in molecular density in proximal versus distal regions (5–30 nm versus 50–200 nm from the PoSM) of cytoplasm in the postsynaptic compartment (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the molecular density analysis shown in Figure 1H.

claim: A higher density of proteins characteristic of the PSD is not a conserved feature with adult mouse brain glutamatergic synapses.
source: These data suggest that a higher density of proteins characteristic of the PSD is not a conserved feature with adult mouse brain glutamatergic synapses (Tao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the molecular density data with reference to a previous study.

claim: 93 ultra-fresh synapse tomograms were collected from 5 mice.
source: 93 ultra-fresh and 50 acute slice/in-tissue (vitreous cryo-section) Psd95-GFP synapse tomograms were collected from 5 and 6 mice, respectively.
evidence: This is a methodological detail describing the dataset size.

claim: 50 in-tissue synapse tomograms were collected from 6 mice.
source: 93 ultra-fresh and 50 acute slice/in-tissue (vitreous cryo-section) Psd95-GFP synapse tomograms were collected from 5 and 6 mice, respectively.
evidence: This is a methodological detail describing the dataset size.

claim: Less than half the population of in-tissue synapses contained a significant relative increase in molecular density in regions of the cytoplasm proximal to the PoSM.
source: Less than half the population of synapses contained a significant relative increase in molecular density in regions of the cytoplasm proximal to the PoSM (5–30 nm versus 50–200 nm from the PoSM, Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the molecular density analysis of in-tissue synapses shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The variability of molecular crowding in near-physiological in-tissue synapses was consistent with the ultra-fresh synapse tomograms.
source: The variability of molecular crowding in these near-physiological in-tissue synapses was consistent with the ultra-fresh synapse tomograms, indicating that the presence of even a slight increase in cytoplasmic molecular density that could correspond to a PSD was not a conserved feature of glutamatergic synapses.
evidence: This is an interpretation comparing the two datasets.

claim: Conventional EM of acute slice brain samples and ultra-fresh synapses showed a PSD in samples from Dlg4GFP/GFP comparable to those in wild-type mice.
source: To rule out that the absence of a conserved postsynaptic protein dense region was caused by the Dlg4GFP/GFP knock-in mutation or the method of sample preparation, we performed conventional EM of acute slice brain samples and ultra-fresh synapses, which showed a PSD in samples from Dlg4GFP/GFP comparable to those in wild-type mice (Figure 2G-H, Figure 2—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is a control experiment shown in Figure 2G-H and Figure 2—figure supplement 7.

claim: The appearance of the high local protein density that defines the PSD is a consequence of conventional EM sample preparation methods.
source: This confirmed that the appearance of the high local protein density that defines the PSD is a consequence of conventional EM sample preparation methods.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the control experiment comparing cryoET and conventional EM.

claim: At least one membrane-bound organelle was present in 61 ± 4% of PoSM compartments.
source: At least one membrane-bound organelle was present in 61 ± 4% of PoSM compartments and, excluding synaptic vesicles, in 77 ± 2% of PreSM compartments (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the organelle analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Excluding synaptic vesicles, at least one membrane-bound organelle was present in 77 ± 2% of PreSM compartments.
source: At least one membrane-bound organelle was present in 61 ± 4% of PoSM compartments and, excluding synaptic vesicles, in 77 ± 2% of PreSM compartments (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the organelle analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Mitochondria were most abundantly found in the presynaptic compartment (44 ± 5% of PreSM).
source: Mitochondria were also readily identified, most abundantly in the presynaptic compartment (44 ± 5% of PreSM) and only once in close proximity to the postsynaptic compartment (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the organelle analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claim: All presynaptic mitochondria contained amorphous dense aggregates within the mitochondrial matrix.
source: A striking feature of all presynaptic mitochondria was the presence of amorphous dense aggregates within the mitochondrial matrix (Figure 3—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is a finding from the cryoET data analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Similar mitochondrial aggregates have been identified as solid deposits of calcium phosphate.
source: Similar aggregates have been identified as solid deposits of calcium phosphate (Wolf et al., 2017) and are apparent in cultured neurons (Tao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Mitochondrial granular aggregates likely represent a physiologically normal feature of the mammalian brain.
source: These data showed synapses with mitochondrial aggregates in the absence of exogenous calcium, suggesting they do not arise during sample preparation. Thus, mitochondrial granular aggregates likely represent a physiologically normal feature of the mammalian brain, which is in keeping with the role of synaptic mitochondria as a reservoir of cellular calcium ions (Billups and Forsythe, 2002).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data with reference to a previous study on mitochondrial function.

claim: The volume of the PoSM compartment ranged from 3x10^6 to 79x10^6 nm^3.
source: The volume of the PoSM compartment in our dataset ranged from 3x106 to 79x106 nm3.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the 3D segmentation analysis.

claim: The size of PoSM compartments was not correlated with the amount of Psd95-GFP detected by cryoCLEM.
source: In keeping with the known diversity of Psd95-containing synapses (Zhu et al., 2018) and in vivo fluorescence imaging experiments (Melander et al., 2021), the size of PoSM compartments was not correlated with the amount of Psd95-GFP detected by cryoCLEM (p=0.7, Pearson's r=0.06, Figure 3E; Melander et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 3E, with reference to previous studies.

claim: The size of PoSM compartments was correlated with the number of actin cytoskeletal filaments.
source: However, the size of PoSM compartments was correlated with the number of actin cytoskeletal filaments (p<0.0001, Pearson's r=0.83, Figure 3F)
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 3F.

claim: In 32 ± 6% synapses, pit-like, hemifusion or hemifission structures were identified in the membrane.
source: In 32 ± 6% synapses we identified pit-like, hemifusion or hemifission structures in the membrane (Figure 3—figure supplement 1J) that likely indicate intermediates of membrane remodeling trapped within the sample at the moment of freezing (Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the membrane remodeling analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1J.

claim: Significantly more remodeling intermediates were identified in the PreSM compared to PoSM compartments.
source: Significantly more remodeling intermediates were identified in the PreSM compared to PoSM compartments (Figure 3G, Paired two-tailed t-test, p=0.021, n=5 mice)
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the statistical analysis shown in Figure 3G.

claim: In 21 ± 11% of tomograms, a clathrin coat was unambiguously identified.
source: In a subset of tomograms (21 ± 11%, Figure 3H), a clathrin coat was unambiguously identified by the triskelion-forming pentagonal and hexagonal openings (Kanaseki and Kadota, 1969; Kravčenko et al., 2024) evident in the raw tomographic maps (Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the clathrin coat analysis shown in Figure 3H, with reference to previous studies.

claim: The average cleft height was 33 nm.
source: The PreSM to PoSM distances across the cleft indicated an average cleft height of 33 nm (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the cleft height analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Average cleft heights of ~20 nm have been determined in non-native conditions by conventional EM.
source: These values differ from average cleft heights of ~20 nm determined in non-native conditions by conventional EM (Peters et al., 1970)
evidence: This is a comparison to previous conventional EM studies.

claim: The average cleft height values are consistent with super-resolution light microscopy imaging.
source: These values differ from average cleft heights of ~20 nm determined in non-native conditions by conventional EM (Peters et al., 1970) but are consistent with super-resolution light microscopy imaging (Tønnesen et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous super-resolution microscopy studies.

claim: The average cleft height of each synapse varied, ranging from 27 to 37 nm.
source: Interestingly, the average cleft height of each synapse in our dataset varied (ranging from 27 to 37 nm).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the cleft height analysis.

claim: Putative ionotropic glutamate receptors were readily identified in 95 ± 2% of PoSM compartments.
source: Putative ionotropic glutamate receptors were readily identified in 95 ± 2% of PoSM compartments.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the receptor identification analysis.

claim: 2,522 receptors were manually picked for subtomogram averaging.
source: To confirm the identity of these proteins, we manually picked 2,522 receptors and extracted sub-volumes at those positions.
evidence: This is a methodological detail describing the subtomogram averaging procedure.

claim: Subtomogram averaging gave a 25 Å resolution 'Y' shaped cryoEM density map extending 14 nm from the PoSM.
source: We then applied subtomogram averaging procedures (see methods), which gave a 25 Å resolution 'Y' shaped cryoEM density map extending 14 nm from the PoSM (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from the subtomogram averaging analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The atomic structure of the AMPA receptor was well accommodated by the subtomogram averaging density.
source: Consequently, the atomic structure of the AMPA receptor was well accommodated by the density, which supports the identification of these ion channels within our synapse tomogram dataset (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a finding from the model fitting analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Clusters were identified in 78% of synapses with an average of 2 clusters per synapse.
source: Clusters were identified in 78% of synapses with an average of 2 clusters per synapse (Figure 4D)
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the cluster analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Receptor clusters were composed of up to 60 ionotropic glutamate receptors with an average of 10 receptors per cluster.
source: Clusters were identified in 78% of synapses with an average of 2 clusters per synapse (Figure 4D), which were composed of up to 60 ionotropic glutamate receptors (average 10 receptors per cluster) (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the cluster analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: 60% of synapses maintained multiple large clusters of ionotropic glutamate receptors completely or partly outside of the cleft.
source: We, therefore, analyzed the distribution of clusters in the context of the overall synapse architecture, which revealed that 60% of synapses maintained multiple large clusters of ionotropic glutamate receptors completely or partly outside of the cleft (Figure 4D–F).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the cluster distribution analysis shown in Figure 4D–F.

claim: The apparent detection of perisynaptic populations of glutamate receptors resembles the distributions observed by previous freeze-fracture immunogold EM.
source: The apparent detection of perisynaptic populations of glutamate receptors resemble the distributions observed by previous freeze-fracture immunogold EM (Masugi-Tokita and Shigemoto, 2007) and super-resolution light microscopy (Nair et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous studies using different techniques.

claim: The PSD has been a defining structure of glutamatergic synapses and has been most frequently observed by conventional EM.
source: The PSD has been a defining structure of glutamatergic synapses and has been most frequently observed by conventional EM (Bourne and Harris, 2008; Sheng and Kim, 2011), including when using more recent methods that involve freeze-substitution into organic solvents, followed by heavy-metal staining (Chen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with citations to previous studies.

claim: The appearance of a PSD in room temperature EM experiments could arise during sample preparation.
source: We, therefore, suggest that the appearance of a PSD in room temperature EM experiments could arise during sample preparation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the comparison between cryoET and conventional EM data.

claim: Preferential heavy-metal staining, crosslinking of interacting proteins by fixatives, or extraction of cytoplasmic proteins could alter the apparent local distribution or relative density of proteins in tissue samples prepared by resin-embedding and freeze-substitution EM methods.
source: Preferential heavy-metal staining, crosslinking of interacting proteins by fixatives, or extraction of cytoplasmic proteins that are not directly or indirectly associated with the postsynaptic membrane could alter the apparent local distribution or relative density of proteins in tissue samples prepared by resin-embedding and freeze-substitution EM methods.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the differences observed between cryoET and conventional EM.

claim: Pioneering cryoET work of synapses purified from brain (synaptosomes) suggested a slightly higher relative molecular density juxtaposed to the postsynaptic membrane.
source: Pioneering cryoET work of synapses purified from brain (synaptosomes) suggested a slightly higher relative molecular density juxtaposed to the postsynaptic membrane (Fernández-Busnadiego et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a citation to a previous cryoET study.

claim: The marked absence of microtubules in synaptosomes is indicative of sample deterioration.
source: Indeed, the marked absence of microtubules in synaptosomes is indicative of sample deterioration.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known instability of microtubules.

claim: Recent cryoCLEM and cryoET studies of primary neuronal cell cultures identified glutamatergic synapses with some but not all showing a subtly higher concentration of macromolecules juxtaposed to the PoSM relative to distal regions.
source: More recent cryoCLEM and cryoET studies of primary neuronal cell cultures identified glutamatergic synapses with some but not all showing a subtly higher concentration of macromolecules juxtaposed to the PoSM relative to distal regions deep within the postsynaptic compartment (Tao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a citation to a previous cryoET study of cultured neurons.

claim: A greater fraction of ultra-fresh adult synapses resembled the minority of primary neuronal synapses that lacked a relative increase in molecular crowding at the PoSM.
source: A greater fraction of ultra-fresh adult synapses resembled the minority of primary neuronal synapses that lacked a relative increase in molecular crowding at the PoSM.
evidence: This is a comparison between the current study and previous work on cultured neurons.

claim: In anatomically intact brain slice preparations that were nearer to the physiological state of adult brain, even fewer instances of synapses were observed with a relative increase in molecular crowding of the cytoplasm at the PoSM.
source: In anatomically intact brain slice preparations that were nearer to the physiological state of adult brain, even fewer instances of synapses were observed with a relative increase in molecular crowding of the cytoplasm at the PoSM.
evidence: This is a finding from the in-tissue synapse analysis.

claim: These subtle differences of molecular crowding are likely a consequence of synapse heterogeneity or the source of central synapses.
source: We suggest that these subtle differences of molecular crowding are likely a consequence of synapse heterogeneity (Zhu et al., 2018) or the source, in vitro cell culture versus adult brain, of central synapses.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed variability with reference to previous work.

claim: A relatively higher concentration of proteins juxtaposed to the PoSM is neither conserved nor a defining feature of glutamatergic synapses.
source: More broadly, these cryoET data were consistent in suggesting that a relatively higher concentration of proteins juxtaposed to the PoSM is neither conserved nor a defining feature of glutamatergic synapses.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cryoET data analysis.

claim: The synaptic architectures reported here were consistent with the existence of specialized protein nanodomains of particular synaptic constituents detected by fluorescence labeling, including Psd95.
source: The synaptic architectures reported here were nevertheless consistent with the existence of specialized protein nanodomains of particular synaptic constituents detected by fluorescence labeling, including Psd95 (Broadhead et al., 2016; Dani et al., 2010; MacGillavry et al., 2013; Nair et al., 2013; Tang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement of consistency with previous fluorescence microscopy studies.

claim: Cleft height was highly variable and on average 65% greater than that observed by conventional EM.
source: Cleft height was highly variable and on average 65% greater than that observed by conventional EM, which is also likely explained by the harsh treatments and the well-characterised shrinkage associated with chemical fixation of tissues in conventional EM.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the cleft height analysis with an interpretation.

claim: The arrangement of prominent constituents appeared to define the architecture of each glutamatergic synapse.
source: Notwithstanding the absence of a conserved PSD, the arrangement of prominent constituents, including branched F-actin networks, organelles, ionotropic glutamate receptors, and transsynaptic adhesion complexes, appeared to define the architecture of each glutamatergic synapse.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed structural features.

claim: The apparent variability of molecular and membrane architectures is in keeping with the enormous diversity of glutamatergic synapse types in the mammalian brain.
source: Overall, the apparent variability of molecular and membrane architectures, from one synapse tomogram to the next, is in keeping with the enormous diversity of glutamatergic synapse types in the mammalian brain (Zhu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed variability with reference to previous work.

claim: Animals were treated in accordance with the UK Animal Scientific Procedures Act (1986) and NIH and ARRIVE guidelines.
source: Animals were treated in accordance with the UK Animal Scientific Procedures Act (1986) and NIH and ARRIVE guidelines.
evidence: This is a statement of ethical compliance.

claim: All animal experiments were approved by the University of Leeds Animal Welfare and Ethics Committee.
source: All animal experiments were approved by the University of Leeds Animal Welfare and Ethics Committee.
evidence: This is a statement of ethical approval.

claim: The endogenous Psd95 protein levels, assembly into supercomplexes, anatomical localization, developmental timing of expression and electrophysiological function in the hippocampus CA1-CA3 synapses in Dlg4GFP mice are indistinguishable from WT mice.
source: The endogenous Psd95 protein levels, assembly into supercomplexes, anatomical localization, developmental timing of expression and electrophysiological function in the hippocampus CA1-CA3 synapses in Dlg4GFP mice are indistinguishable from WT mice (Broadhead et al., 2016; Frank et al., 2016; Zhu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a characterization of the mouse model with citations to previous studies.

claim: Ice-cold ACSF was used to limit mechanical stimulation since synaptic transmission and other enzyme-catalyzed processes are negligible at this temperature.
source: Ice-cold ACSF was used to limit mechanical stimulation since synaptic transmission and other enzyme-catalyzed processes (e.g. endocytosis) are negligible at this temperature (Volgushev et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a methodological rationale with a citation to a previous study.

claim: Psd95 is a membrane-associated cytoplasmic protein that concentrates exclusively within mature glutamatergic synapses.
source: Psd95 is a membrane-associated cytoplasmic protein that concentrates exclusively within mature glutamatergic synapses (Chen et al., 2000; El Husseini et al., 2000)
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with citations to previous studies.

claim: Psd95 forms supercomplexes with ionotropic glutamate receptors that reside in the postsynaptic membrane.
source: Psd95 is a membrane-associated cytoplasmic protein that concentrates exclusively within mature glutamatergic synapses (Chen et al., 2000; El Husseini et al., 2000) and forms supercomplexes with ionotropic glutamate receptors that reside in the postsynaptic membrane (Frank et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge with a citation to a previous study.

claim: The GFP signal from Dlg4GFP/GFP knockin mice pinpoints the location of mature glutamatergic synapses without over-expression or any detectable effect on synapse function.
source: The GFP signal from Dlg4GFP/GFP knockin mice pinpoints the location of mature glutamatergic synapses without over-expression or any detectable effect on synapse function (Broadhead et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a characterization of the mouse model with a citation to a previous study.

claim: Psd95-GFP puncta resembled those observed by confocal fluorescent imaging of the brain.
source: Thus, cryoEM grids were imaged on a cryogenic fluorescence microscope (cryoFM), revealing Psd95-GFP puncta (Figure 1B), absent in WT control samples (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), which resembled those observed by confocal fluorescent imaging of the brain (Zhu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous confocal imaging studies shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CryoCLEM images showed Psd95-GFP puncta that were invariably associated with membrane-bound subcellular compartments (100–1300 nm diameter).
source: Using a cryoCLEM workflow, the same grids were then imaged by cryoEM, and fluorescent Psd95-GFP puncta were mapped onto the cryoEM image (Figure 1B). These cryoCLEM images showed Psd95-GFP puncta that were invariably associated with membrane-bound subcellular compartments (100–1300 nm diameter) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from the cryoCLEM analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Docked synaptic vesicles were defined as vesicles connected 2–8 nm from the PreSM via macromolecular tethers.
source: Docked synaptic vesicles were defined as vesicles connected 2–8 nm from the PreSM via macromolecular tethers.
evidence: This is a methodological definition used in the analysis.

claim: The average diameter of synaptic vesicles was 40.2 nm.
source: The average diameter of synaptic vesicles was 40.2 nm and the minimum and maximum dimensions ranged from 20–57.8 nm, measured from the outside of the vesicle that included ellipsoidal synaptic vesicles similar to those previously reported (Tao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the vesicle size analysis with a comparison to a previous study.

claim: No significant difference was observed comparing synapses from the cortex versus hippocampus.
source: No significant difference was observed comparing synapses from the cortex versus hippocampus, as expected (Zhu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a finding from the statistical analysis with a reference to previous work.

claim: CryoET data from vitreous cryo-sections can reveal in-tissue protein structures at subnanometer and near-atomic resolution.
source: We and others have recently shown that cryoET data from vitreous cryo-sections can reveal in-tissue protein structures at subnanometer and near-atomic resolution (Gilbert et al., 2024; Elferich et al., 2025).
evidence: This is a statement about recent technical advances with citations to recent studies.

claim: CryoFIB-milling has the advantage of overcoming the local knife damage caused by cryo-sectioning.
source: While cryoFIB-milling has the advantage of overcoming the local knife damage caused by cryo-sectioning, it introduces amorphization across the whole sample that diminishes the information content (Al-Amoudi et al., 2005; Lovatt et al., 2022; Lucas and Grigorieff, 2023).
evidence: This is a comparison of different sample preparation methods with citations to previous studies.

claim: Several reports of synapse cryoET from within cultured primary neurons and mouse brain were prepared by cryoFIB-milling.
source: Since submission of our manuscript, several reports of synapse cryoET from within cultured primary neurons (Held et al., 2024a; Held et al., 2024b) and mouse brain (Glynn et al., 2024; Matsui et al., 2024) were prepared by cryoFIB-milling.
evidence: This is a citation to recent related studies.

claim: These new datasets are largely consistent with the data reported here.
source: These new datasets are largely consistent with the data reported here.
evidence: This is a comparison to recent related studies.
